Amazon Web Services is down, taking a big chunk of the internet with it

Published 2026-10-07 09:55 UTC

If your apps are not loading this morning, you are not alone: Amazon Web Services is having a major outage. Slack, Venmo, Ring doorbells, Fortnite, Duolingo and even some of Amazon's own services, including Alexa, are failing or loading slowly.

Amazon's AWS Health Dashboard says it is investigating increased error rates in the US-EAST-1 region, which covers data centers in northern Virginia. The problem appears to have started with DynamoDB, Amazon's database service, before spreading to EC2 and Lambda.

Downdetector shows millions of outage reports. AWS says it is seeing signs of recovery, but warns that a backlog of requests means some services will stay degraded for hours. We will update this story as services return.

By mid-morning, outage trackers showed tens of thousands of reports for services that rely on Amazon's cloud. Slack messages failed to send, Venmo payments stalled, and Ring doorbells stopped sending alerts to phones. Several popular games, including Fortnite, kicked players out of matches and prevented new logins. Some airline check-in systems and food delivery apps also had problems.

Amazon's status page acknowledged increased error rates and latencies for multiple services in the US-EAST-1 region, located in northern Virginia. That region is the company's oldest and largest, and many companies run critical systems there by default. Engineers who build on the platform said the incident shows again how much of the internet depends on a single region.

Amazon said it had identified the cause and was applying mitigations, though recovery was gradual because services had to work through backlogs of queued requests. Some customers reported that dashboards and support tools hosted in the same region were also unavailable, making it harder to diagnose their own systems.

Companies that had set up their systems to fail over to other regions recovered faster. Analysts said the outage will likely prompt more businesses to invest in multi-region architectures, though doing so adds cost and complexity that many smaller firms cannot easily absorb.
